text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 4 in history.
1307 - The Swiss Confederation declared itself independent of Austria.
1520 - Christian II of Denmark was crowned King of Sweden, and granted an amnesty to his opponents.
1605 - In London, Guy Fawkes was arrested under the House of Commons preparing gunpowder to blow up the building when Parliament re-assembled the next day.
1650 - King William III of England born in The Hague. Known as William of Orange, he became king in 1689 and during his reign reconquered Ireland.
1740 - Augustus Toplady, British clergyman and writer of hymns including "Rock of Ages", born.
1847 - Felix Mendelssohn, German composer and pianist, died in Leipzig.
1854 - Florence Nightingale and a team of 38 nurses arrived in the Crimea to set up a hospital for British troops at Scutari.
1862 - The first rapid-fire machine gun was patented by Richard Jordan Gatling in Indianapolis, and named after him.
1879 - Will Rogers, U.S. actor, humorist and author, born.
1890 - The first electrified underground railway system was officially opened in London.
1916 - Walter Cronkite, U.S. broadcaster and journalist who anchored the CBS television evening news for 20 years, born.
1917 - Gig Young born as Byron Barr. He played a character called Gig Young in the 1941 film "The Gay Sisters" and thereafter used the name.
1918 - The allied powers in the First World War agreed on peace terms for Germany based on U.S. President Wilson's "Fourteen Points".
1921 - Takashi Hara, prime minister of Japan, was assassinated by a rightist fanatic.
1936 - Didier Ratsiraka, Malagasy statesman and president of Madagascar 1975-93, born.
1942 - British troops defeated the Germans under General Rommel at El Alamein after a 12-day battle.
1946 - The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) was formed.
1952 - Dwight D. Eisenhower was elected president of the United States.
1956 - Soviet troops moved in to crush the Hungarian uprising. Imre Nagy was ousted as prime minister and replaced by Janos Kadar.
1966 - The worst floods in Italy's history affected a third of the country. Florence was cut off and many of the city's art treasures were damaged.
1977 - The U.N. imposed a mandatory ban on arms supplies to South Africa in an effort to force the country out of Namibia.
1979 - Iranian militants seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran and captured 90 hostages; 52 were held captive for 444 days.
1980 - Ronald Reagan was elected president of the United States.
1982 - The U.N. passed a resolution calling on Argentina and Britain to discuss sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.
1983 - In Lebanon, over 40 Israeli soldiers were killed when an Arab suicide bomber drove a truck full of explosives into their camp.
1988 - An attempted coup by foreign mercenaries on the Maldive Islands was thwarted when Indian paratroopers crushed the revolt.
1995 - Yigal Amir, who said he was acting on God's orders, assassinated Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin as he left a peace rally in Tel Aviv.
